subject: Post-call: Reliability & graceful-deg qualification — Finovate Capital
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Kumar <sanjay.kumar@finovatecap.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@finovatecap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: Post-call: Reliability & graceful-deg qualification — Finovate Capital

Thanks for the time this afternoon — appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap from my side and concrete next steps so we stay aligned.

High-level pain points you shared
- Outages over last 6 months impacting checkout suggestions (2 incidents; 1x full region fail, 1x model OOM under traffic spike).
- No automated fallback currently; on-call triage is manual and takes ~18–24 mins to route traffic.
- Cost pressure on inference fleet; team reluctant to run overprovisioned replicas.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Primary: private AWS VPC in us-east-1 running 8x G4dn-based serving instances behind an autoscaler.
- Model family: a tuned open LLM (retail-suggest-v2) with custom prompt layers; KV cache in Redis.
- Observability: Datadog + in-house alerting; limited per-request token cost breakdown.

Success criteria you described
- 99.9% availability for inference endpoints (monthly), p95 latency < 300ms for 512-token infer requests, and <5% error-rate during peak windows.
- Failover from us-east-1 to us-west-2 (warm standby) within 3 minutes for regional outages.
- Measurable cost reduction target: 20% per-token inference cost in production vs today during steady state.

Proposed graceful-deg strategy (initial scope)
1) Prefetch + prefix KV caching for common checkout prompts to cut tokens and latency.
2) Multi-tier model routing: primary high-quality model -> quantized variant (reduced perf/cost) -> embeddings-only fallback for degraded mode.
3) Region failover plan: active us-east-1, warm us-west-2 (KV sync cadence, DNS TTLs, and routing playbook).
4) Circuit-breaker with throttled responses and cached answers for short-duration overloads.

Open technical questions we need from you
- Can you share the most recent incident timeline (postmortem) and the rough traffic curve for the two incidents?
- What is your current KV cache hit rate and Redis scaling limits?
- Any hard SLA commitments to merchants we should be aware of (penalty clauses)?

Next steps (agreed)
- Logan/Redwood: deliver a preliminary SLO matrix + graceful-deg runbook template by EOD Mon (attached SLO-matrix-template.xlsx).
- Finovate: share the last incident postmortem and network/VPC peering diagram by EOD Wed.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra and platform on Tue 8/18 — 60 minutes (Logan to send invite).

Attachments: SLO-matrix-template.xlsx (template), SOC2-evidence-request.pdf (checklist we typically ask during Private deployments).

Cheers,

Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

--

Thanks, Logan — this is exactly the kind of framing we needed. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Incident notes: I'll drop the two postmortems into the shared drive by EOD tomorrow. The region fail was caused by a bad AMI push that took the autoscaler offline; the OOM was a memory regression tied to a dependency bump during a traffic spike.
- Our merchants expect <1 minute perceived downtime for checkout; contractual penalties kick in for multi-minute outages (we don't have a hard $ SLA published but it's effectively enforced).
- Redis hit rate is ~68% for popular keys; the cache is a single AZ cluster today (we know that's an exposure).

Also happy to confirm Tue 8/18 16:00 ET for the deep-dive — please send the calendar invite.

Sanjay Kumar
VP, Platform Engineering
